messages:
maya (Support): heads up — escalated from Acme: their prod keys hit a bunch of 429s and auth failures during our internal surge sim yesterday. customer saw billing spikes too. sending repro steps.

jess (customer): confirmed — we got ~30% errored responses, several 401s followed by retries that drove usage. our team paused the test.

maya (Support): repro notes pasted below. requesting SRE help to validate whether this is quota exhaustion vs a bug in token handling. @ryan can you triage?

jess (customer): repro commands we used: `heyload --keys $APIKEY --pattern burst --rps 200 --duration 10m` — also used short retry backoff on 401s.

ryan (eng-sre): pinged. quick q: was this against Hosted or Dedicated? and were the requests hitting multiple models/route variants?

maya (Support): Hosted (us-east). single model route, generation endpoint, mostly short prompts (avg 60 tokens).

deploy-bot: [alert] 03/28 16:02:12 — rate_limit_exceeded on api-gen-v1 (us-east) — window=60s, keys=74, burst=150

ryan (eng-sre): looks like key-level burst was high but sustained RPM pushed them into token bucket depletion. two things to do: 1) reproduce with our lab to confirm behavior; 2) collect request-id traces + auth logs for that key. Maya can you share request-ids?

maya (Support): pasted request ids in thread DMs — also attaching truncated logs in S3: s3://redwood-triage/acme/20240328/trace.tar.gz

sara (eng-infra): for lab repro I recommend a two-phase test: ramp to target RPS over 2m, hold for 8m, then sudden 2x spike for 30s. use concurrent clients to emulate retries. example ab-style: `wrk -t12 -c200 -d600s --latency http://api.redwood/v1/gen` but with our header for API key.

ryan (eng-sre): add these checks in the script: log 429 vs 401 counts separately, capture X-RateLimit-* headers, and extract cache-hit header (prefix caching). if 401s appear only during bursts that implies auth path is overloaded or token cache eviction.

todd (product): curious: why did customer see billing spike? If retries are immediate on 401s they double-count requests. we should test retry policy effect. maya, did they use exponential backoff?

jess (customer): default client retried immediately up to 3 times with jitter; we didn't throttle retries.

sara (eng-infra): OK — two failure modes to validate: (A) quota/rate-limit token bucket exhaustion (expected) and (B) auth-handling/backoff causing duplicate billable attempts. lab plan should measure billable request count vs successful responses.

ryan (eng-sre): I'm going to run a quick lab with a synthetic key that mirrors hosted defaults. hypothesis: our default per-key burst (burst tokens) is too permissive for shared infra, causing downstream exhaustion when many keys spike simultaneously. test will sweep per-key RPM: [60, 120, 300, 600] and burst windows [1s, 10s, 60s].

maya (Support): timeline? customer needs guidance on mitigation today.

ryan (eng-sre): short term mitigation: ask customer to cap client-side max concurrent requests to 50 and add exponential backoff (500ms -> 2s). I'll also temporarily bump their dedicated quota if available — ping infra.

sara (eng-infra): I can provision a sandpit with traffic shaping. will also run an internal multi-key storm to see systemic effects. plan: 1) single-key sweep to map RPM->error curve, 2) 100-key simultaneous spike to measure tail impacts.

todd (product): from a defaults standpoint we should aim for safe defaults that minimize collateral damage for noisy customers. idea: default per-key RPM = 120 rps-per-minute? (i.e., 2 rps) and default burst window 10s with burst cap at 20 requests. but want data before locking anything.

ryan (eng-sre): agree we need data. my target for default policy will be conservative: prefer lower steady RPM + modest burst to avoid global saturation. will share CSV of sweeps.

maya (Support): I'll draft a troubleshooting reply for Acme with immediate mitigations (client caps + backoff) and ETA for our lab results.

jess (customer): appreciate quick response. we'll pause the test until you confirm.

ryan (eng-sre): running first sweep now. quick note for triage: capture CPU and egress metrics on inference clusters, plus auth service latency. sometimes auth slowdowns cause cascading 401s that clients retry into more load.

sara (eng-infra): started multi-key storm in us-east sandpit (keys=100, hold 5m). monitoring dashboards: token-bucket-fill shows per-node variance — some nodes exhausted earlier due to imbalanced routing. adding sticky hashing to reduce variance for the test.

ryan (eng-sre): results (prelim): single-key at 600 RPM with 60s burst => 40% 429s under sustained 5m hold. 120 RPM with 10s burst => <1% 429s, latency stable. multi-key storm shows tail 99th latency spikes when >30% keys spike simultaneously.

todd (product): that's useful — suggests default steady RPM near 120/min and default burst window 10s is a reasonable starting point. but product question: do we want to expose burst config to customers or hide it behind automatic smoothing?

sara (eng-infra): operational note: sticky routing reduced variance but not eliminated it; we should implement per-node admission control and global fallback to cheaper model variant if node overloaded.

maya (Support): draft reply to customer: short-term mitigations listed + we'll follow up with policy changes. will include recommended client retry backoff example:

```
// JS example
async function callWithBackoff(req) {
  for (let i=0;i<3;i++){
    const res = await fetch(req)
    if (res.status === 401 || res.status === 429) await sleep(2**i * 250 + Math.random()*100)
    else return res
  }
  throw new Error('exhausted retries')
}
```

ryan (eng-sre): next steps: finalize lab sweeps, produce a short doc with recommended sane defaults (steady RPM ranges, burst window sizes, and client retry guidance). will propose these defaults in a PR for rate-limiter config.

todd (product): set milestone: have a proposed default policy + rollout plan by EOW. include rollback criteria and telemetry to watch (rate-limit hits, billing anomalies, auth error spikes).

maya (Support): sending Acme the temporary mitigations now. tagging the thread for follow-up once lab CSV is up.

deploy-bot: [deploy] 03/28 17:05 — created branch rate-defaults/proposal by ryan

ryan (eng-sre): uploaded sweep CSVs to /internal/sweeps/20240328/acme_burst_sweeps.csv and will open the PR with numbers.

sara (eng-infra): after PR we should run staged rollout on a small subset of keys before global defaults change.

maya (Support): thanks team — I think we have an action plan. feel free to add anything I missed.

ryan (eng-sre): ack. will summarize in the PR and ping for reviews.

jess (customer): thanks all, we'll re-run tests after you confirm."
